newsitem.title: MONACO: RALLYING-MAKINEN TAKES COMMAND AS MCRAE CRASHES OUT.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-MAKINEN TAKES COMMAND AS MCRAE CRASHES OUT.

text.p: World champion Tommi Makinen took command in the Monte Carlo rally on Tuesday as Colin McRae crashed out.
Brilliant driving on wet, sometimes icy asphalt in the Vercors mountains allowed Finn Makinen to take first place from overnight leader Carlos Sainz of Spain.
After four of the penultimate day's six timed stages, Makinen, in his Mitsubihi Lancer, was 13 seconds ahead of Sainz's Ford Escort.
McRae, who had dropped to fourth place overall after hitting a snowdrift on Monday, went off the road again in Tuesday's 33-km first stage from St Jean en Royans to La Chapelle en Vercors.

The 1995 world champion broke the rear left supension and damaged the steering of his new Subaru Impreza. He managed to finish the stage but ended it over 24 minutes behind his Subaru team mate Piero Liatti of Italy who clocked the best time.
As technical assistance was prohibited before the start of the next stage, the Scotsman had to pull out.

"We hit a patch of ice on my side and went off into the snowbank," McRae explained. "We lost of a lot of time to get the car out. We managed to finish the stage but the front left steering arm was broken and it was impossible to continue."
The second fastest time, 13 seconds slower than Liatti, was enough to allow Makinen, who had started the day three seconds behind Sainz, to go top.
Sainz, twice a winner of the winter classic, had to be content wiith the third fastest time and lost 18 seconds on his rival in that section.
Liatti and German Armin Schwarz, in a Ford Escrot, took the next two tests with both Makinen and Sainz a few seconds slower.
Then, as sun came out for the first time since the race started from Monte Carlo on Sunday, Makinen was fastest on the 27.47-km stretch from Ruissas to Eygalayes, gaining nine seconds on Sainz.
"There was something wrong with my brakes," said Sainz. "Apart from that, everything's all right. It's not over yet."
Makinen said he had a scare when a warning light showed on his dashboard.
"It kept flashing for the whole stage," he said. "Don't ask me what it was, I just don't know."
